title-slide.en: Welcome to session ten, the last session of Block one.
Today is a clinic. We brief the individual research note, review each other's network plans, and close with quiz two.

route.en: A short brief on the research note, then a peer review and an idea card, and then quiz two for twenty minutes.

block-map.en: Block one followed one company through three questions.
Decision making asked how CellCo should add capacity. The staged build gave a mean NPV of 79 million yuan and a twenty percent chance of loss.
Markov analysis described yield and maintenance over time. The line yield is 0.933, and preventive maintenance pays only in the major-wear state.
The network model asked when the storage system will be ready: a 71 percent chance by 22 weeks, and 19 weeks for 0.425 million yuan of crashing.
Your group assignment repeats this chain with your own data variant, and ends in one board memo.

research-note.en: Each of you also writes an individual research note of two pages.
Apply one Block one method to a decision or process in your own research. State the decision, the data you have or would collect, the model, the assumptions, and what the model cannot tell you.
Half of the grade is for using the method correctly, thirty percent for the quality of your assumptions, and twenty percent for clarity.
A small, correct model of a real decision scores better than a large model with unstated assumptions.

method-match.en: Before you choose a method, test yourself on seven cases from energy research.
Read each case, choose the method that fits best, and read the explanation. Some cases admit a second method; in your note, say why you chose yours.

act1.en: In part one, for fifteen minutes, swap your draft network plan with another group and review it against the six checks on the slide.
Pay particular attention to the on-time probability. It should come from a simulation, not from PERT alone.
In part two, for ten minutes, write a three-sentence idea card for your research note: the decision, the method, and the data. Swap it with a partner, and ask one question about theirs.

quiz2.en: Quiz two covers Markov analysis and the network model, sessions four to nine. Work on your own, on paper, for twenty minutes.

to-block2.en: By the twenty-first of February, submit the group report, the workbook or notebook, the recorded presentation, and your research note. You will receive feedback before Block two.
Block two, on the twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth of March, covers linear programming and statistical quality control, again with CellCo.
Crashing in session eight was already a linear program. Block two starts there. Thank you for your work in Block one.
